IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
(Bail Appl. No.01 of 2025)
In
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025
Rakesh Chaudhary ...Appellant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ...Respondents
With
(Bail Appl. No.01 of 2025)
In
Criminal Appeal No.419 of 2025
Ajay Deopa ...Appellant
Vs.
State of Uttarakhand ...Respondents
Presence: Mr. Devesh Upreti, learned counsel for the Appellants/Applicants.
 Mr. Dinesh Chauhan, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State of 
 Uttarakhand. 
Hon’ble Ashish Naithani, J.
1. These are applications filed on behalf of the Appellants seeking 
suspension of sentence and grant of bail during pendency of Criminal 
Appeal Nos.418 of 2025 and 419 of 2025, arising out of judgment 
dated 05.06.2025 and sentencing order dated 10.06.2025 passed by the 
learned Sessions Judge, Champawat in Sessions Trial No. 04 of 2021. 
2. Since both appeals arise out of the same judgment and the 
applications for suspension of sentence involve common questions, 
they are being heard together and are being decided by this common 
order. The impugned judgment has resulted in conviction of the 
Appellants under Sections 304 Part I, 324 and 352 IPC, with the 
principal sentence being 10 years’ simple imprisonment. 
1
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025, Rakesh Chaudhary Vs State of Uttarakhand with
Ajay Deopa Vs State of Uttarakhand-----
Ashish Naithani J. 3. The case of the State originates from an incident dated 
05.03.2021 within the jurisdiction of Police Station Lohaghat, District 
Champawat, wherein it was alleged that the Appellants along with co￾accused assaulted the victim, resulting ultimately in his death. 
4. An FIR came to be registered on the same day, initially invoking 
serious offences including Section 302 IPC along with allied 
provisions. After investigation, a charge-sheet was submitted and the 
matter was committed to the Court of Sessions. 
5. Charges were framed against the accused persons under Sections 
302, 307, 352 read with Section 34 IPC and Section 4/25 of the Arms 
Act. 
6. Learned Counsel for the Appellants would submit that the present 
applications seek release on bail during pendency of the appeals, and 
the Appellants have a strong prima facie case warranting grant of such 
relief. 
7. It is contended that the appeals raise substantial and arguable 
questions of fact and law, particularly with regard to the correctness of 
conviction under Section 304 Part I IPC and the applicability of Section 
34 IPC. 
8. Learned Counsel would submit that the learned trial court itself 
did not find the case fit for conviction under Section 302 IPC and 
altered the conviction to Section 304 Part I IPC, which indicates that 
2
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025, Rakesh Chaudhary Vs State of Uttarakhand with
Ajay Deopa Vs State of Uttarakhand-----
Ashish Naithani J. the matter is not free from doubt and requires detailed consideration in 
appeal. 
9. It is further submitted that even on a prima facie reading of the 
material on record, the case proceeds on general allegations of assault, 
and the issue of individual role and shared intention remains open for 
consideration. 
10. Learned Counsel would also submit thatthe reliance placed upon 
alleged recovery of weapons and scientific evidence is primarily 
corroborative in nature, and the manner of proof and linkage of such 
material is an issue that would require deeper scrutiny in appeal. 
11. It is also submitted that the Appellants were on bail throughout 
the course of trial and have not misused the liberty granted to them. 
12. Learned Counsel would further submit that the Appellants have 
already undergone a substantial period of incarceration, and 
considering the pendency of appeals, there is no likelihood of early 
disposal. 
13. It is thus contended that continued incarceration of the Appellants 
during pendency of the appeals would cause undue hardship, 
particularly when the appeals involve arguable issues. 
14. On these grounds, it is prayed that the Appellants be enlarged on 
bail during pendency of the appeals. 
15. Per contra, learned AGA for the State would oppose the 
applications and submit that the Appellants have been convicted after a 
3
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025, Rakesh Chaudhary Vs State of Uttarakhand with
Ajay Deopa Vs State of Uttarakhand-----
Ashish Naithani J. full-fledged trial and the findings recorded by the learned trial court are 
based on due appreciation of evidence. 
16. It is submitted that the offence in question resulted in the death of 
a person and the Appellants stand convicted under Section 304 Part I 
IPC, which is a serious offence. 
17. Learned AGA would further submit that the case is supported by 
the testimony of material witnesses, including the injured witness, 
whose presence at the place of occurrence is not in dispute. 
18. It is also contended that the case is supported by recovery of 
weapons and scientific evidence, which prima facie connects the 
accused persons with the occurrence. 
19. Learned AGA would submit that the learned trial court has 
already taken a balanced view, and no case for grant of bail is made 
out. 
20. It is further submitted that in cases involving serious offences 
affecting life, the Appellants do not deserve the benefit of bail merely 
on the ground of pendency of appeal.
21. This Court has heard learned Counsel for the parties and has 
perused the record. 
22. The present applications seek release on bail during pendency of 
the appeals arising out of conviction under Sections 304 Part I, 324 and 
352 IPC. 
4
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025, Rakesh Chaudhary Vs State of Uttarakhand with
Ajay Deopa Vs State of Uttarakhand-----
Ashish Naithani J. 23. At the outset, it is to be noted that while considering such 
applications, this Court is not required to undertake a detailed re￾appreciation of evidence. However, a limited examination is necessary 
to ascertain whether the appeals raise arguable issues and whether 
continued incarceration is justified in the facts of the case. 
24. The learned trial court has not found the case fit for conviction 
under Section 302 IPC and has instead convicted the Appellants under 
Section 304 Part I IPC. This, prima facie, indicates that the question of 
nature of intention and applicability of the appropriate penal provision 
remains an arguable issue in appeal. 
25. From a prima facie reading of the material on record, the case 
proceeds on allegations of a joint assault. At the same time, the issue of 
individual role attribution and the extent of shared intention under 
Section 34 IPC is a matter which would require detailed consideration 
at the stage of final hearing. 
26. The case of the State rests, inter alia, on the testimony of an 
injured witness and supporting material including recovery and 
scientific evidence. Without expressing any final opinion, this Court 
finds that the scope, consistency and evidentiary value of such material 
are issues which are open to examination in appeal. 
27. It is also not in dispute that the Appellants were on bail during the 
course of trial and there is no allegation that they misused the liberty 
granted to them. 
28. The Appellants have already undergone a substantial period of 
incarceration and, having regard to the pendency of criminal appeals, it 
5
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025, Rakesh Chaudhary Vs State of Uttarakhand with
Ajay Deopa Vs State of Uttarakhand-----
Ashish Naithani J. cannot be said that the appeals are likely to be heard in the immediate 
future. 
29. At the same time, the offence in question has resulted in the loss 
of life, and the seriousness of the offence cannot be ignored while 
considering the prayer for bail. 
30. Thus, this Court is required to balance the nature of accusation, 
the manner in which conviction has been recorded, the arguable issues 
raised in appeal, and the period of incarceration already undergone. 
31. Having considered the aforesaid factors, this Court is of the view 
that the case for grant of bail deserves to be considered on the basis of 
the role attributed to each of the Appellants. 
32. Without expressing any final opinion on the merits, this Court 
finds that the case of Appellant Rakesh Chaudhary stands on a 
relatively different footing at this stage, insofar as the question of 
individual role and extent of liability is concerned, which constitutes an 
arguable issue in appeal. 
33. However, insofar as Appellant Ajay Deopa is concerned, 
considering the nature of allegations, the conviction recorded, and the 
overall circumstances, this Court is not inclined to grant bail at this 
stage. 
ORDER
34. The bail application filed on behalf of Appellant Rakesh 
Chaudhary in Criminal Appeal No. 418 of 2025 is allowed. 
6
Criminal Appeal No.418 of 2025, Rakesh Chaudhary Vs State of Uttarakhand with
Ajay Deopa Vs State of Uttarakhand-----
Ashish Naithani J. 35. Let Appellant Rakesh Chaudhary be released on bail during 
pendency of the appeal on his furnishing a personal bond and two 
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of the Court 
concerned. 
36. The Appellant shall appear before the trial court as and when 
required and shall not tamper with evidence or influence witnesses. 
37. The bail application filed on behalf of Appellant -Ajay Deopa in 
Criminal Appeal No.419 of 2025 is rejected.
38. List these criminal appeals on 16.06.2026. 
(Ashish Naithani J.)
 09.04.2026
